newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW - Pharmacia & Upjohn sees Q4 growth.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Pharmacia & Upjohn sees Q4 growth.

text.p: U.S.-Swedish drugs group Pharmacia & Upjohn said on Thursday it expected to resume its earnings growth in the fourth quarter of the year, after a setback in the three months to September 30.

Executive vice president and chief financial officer Bob Salisbury said in a telephone interview with Reuters that after a "flat" third quarter "we'd expect to have fairly nice growth in the fourth quarter."
Earlier the newly-formed company said third quarter earnings per share fell to 39 cents from 44 cents a year before, after a five cent charge for restructuring and merger costs.
Salisbury said the result was "right in line" with its profit warning three weeks ago, which led analysts to downgrade estimates for the rest of the year and 1997.
He said the company had suffered a "temporary setback" mainly due to unfavourable foreign currency exchange rates, but added "we expect a very nice improvement from the lower base."

He denied that Pharmacia & Upjohn's forecasts of $500 million of annual cost savings from the merger by 1998 had been unrealistic. "Cost savings are coming through at about the same rate as we expected and analysts expected," he said, with some $425 million of this seen in place next year.
Salisbury added that these savings would help to drive the targeted improvement in operating profit margins to 25 percent of sales in 1998 from 18 percent in 1995.

Pharmacia & Upjohn said the flow of new products would also help its performance. It said that since its $6.9 billion merger last year, it had filed 14 regulatory applications for new drugs and product extensions and received 15 marketing clearances.

Salisbury highlighted the potential of cancer drug Camptosar and glaucoma product Xalatan, both launched in the third quarter. He said take-up of Camptosar for colo-rectal cancer was promising, and it is being tested for use in other cancers.

He addeed that Xalatan had already taken a 12 percent market share since its launch in the U.S, adding "we think it has very great promise." Opthalmology sales rose 16 percent to $78 million in the third quarter.
The launch of Camptosar helped to drive a 15 percent improvement in third-quarter sales of cancer drugs to $164 million.
Salisbury played down speculation that the merger of Sweden's Pharmacia with Upjohn of the U.S. had proved more difficult than expected, and led to a clash of cultures.
"I think the issue is not so much specific cultures as bringing together two very different companies" and imposing "a style which is new to both," he said. "It's a big task."

He also reaffirmed the group's commitment to keeping its international headquarters in Britain, noting that it had just taken a 13-year lease on a new building in Windsor, just outside London. Swedish staff were unsettled earlier this year by rumours that the group could shift its international base to New York.
The company expected to see the lease out, Salisbury added.
